p: A bit of organising goes a long way with a group night out, and Flight Club is no different. Book your oche for the right number of players, and if your group is on the bigger side, ask about splitting across neighbouring oches so everyone gets plenty of throws. Arriving a few minutes early means you can grab a drink and settle in before your time starts, rather than rushing straight in.

If you've never played darts properly, here's a quick tip that helps. Stand side-on with your throwing foot forward, keep your elbow still and let your forearm do the work. Aim, release smoothly and follow through towards the board. You won't become a pro overnight, but you'll hit the board a lot more often.

Beyond the darts, Birmingham city centre is packed with things to do. The Library of Birmingham, with its striking gold-and-silver facade, has outdoor terraces with views across the city. Victoria Square and Chamberlain Square are just around the corner, with grand civic buildings and the Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery nearby. For a stroll, the canals around Brindleyplace and Gas Street Basin are a lovely way to see a different side of the city.
Want to make a weekend of it? Brum's food scene is a big part of the fun, from Balti to fine dining. Pair a darts night with a good meal and you've got the perfect city break.
